questions.prompt: What are the **three pillars of observability**?

options.text: **Metrics** (aggregated numbers over time), **Logs** (structured discrete events), and **Traces** (end-to-end request spans)

questions.prompt: Why are **structured logs** (JSON with `timestamp`, `level`, `request_id`, `user_id`) far better than unstructured print strings in production?

options.text: They are machine-parseable, filterable, and correlatable across services by `request_id` / `trace_id`

questions.prompt: Why is **p99 latency** tracked alongside average (mean) latency?

options.text: p99 is always smaller than the median
Averages hide tail-latency spikes experienced by your slowest 1% of requests (often power users or cascading timeouts)

questions.prompt: What are the **Four Golden Signals** of monitoring (Google SRE)?
Select all practices that reduce **alert fatigue** for on-call engineers. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Ensure every paging alert links to an actionable runbook
Deduplicate and group related alerts during cascading failures
Page the entire company for informational warnings
Alert on user-impacting **symptoms** (SLO burn rate / error spikes), not every minor CPU blip

questions.prompt: In **Incident Response**, what is the primary job of the **Incident Commander (IC)**?

options.text: Blaming the author of the last commit
Coordinating roles, decisions, status updates, and escalation while keeping the response focused

questions.prompt: What defines a **blameless postmortem**?

options.text: Focusing on *systemic, tooling, and process* gaps rather than punishing individuals, so teams surface truth honestly

questions.prompt: What is an **error budget** in SRE?

options.text: `100% - SLO` — the acceptable amount of unreliability (e.g., 0.1% for a 99.9% SLO) balancing feature velocity and stability

questions.prompt: Why is **100% availability** almost never the right SLO target?

options.text: The marginal cost and feature-velocity freeze required to go from 99.99% to 100% is astronomical and users rarely notice beyond their own network reliability

questions.prompt: Match each SRE / security concept to its role.

columns.label: Quantifies allowable unreliability to gate risky releases
Stacks independent security controls so one breach isn't fatal

questions.prompt: What is **toil** in Site Reliability Engineering?

options.text: Manual, repetitive, automatable, tactical ops work that scales linearly with service growth and adds no lasting value

questions.prompt: Why must **secrets** (API keys, DB passwords, signing keys) NEVER be logged or committed to Git?

options.text: Git history and log streams persist widely, letting anyone with read access compromise production systems

questions.prompt: What is a **circuit breaker** in distributed reliability?

options.text: A hardware fuse in a laptop
A wrapper that trips open after repeated downstream failures, failing fast to prevent cascading thread/connection exhaustion

questions.prompt: Why should retries against a failing service ALWAYS use **exponential backoff + jitter**?

options.text: Without backoff and random jitter, all clients retry in synchronized waves ('thundering herd'), keeping the service down

questions.prompt: What does **context / deadline propagation** across microservices prevent?

options.text: A caller timing out after 2s while downstream services keep burning CPU/DB for 30s on an abandoned request

questions.prompt: What is **capacity planning**?

options.text: Measuring resource utilization vs traffic growth, load testing limits, and provisioning headroom before saturation hits
Guessing server count once at launch

questions.prompt: What does **high cardinality** in metrics labels (e.g., putting raw `user_id` or `request_id` on Prometheus labels) cause?

options.text: Explosion of time-series count, exhausting monitoring memory and slowing queries

questions.prompt: In **Security Hardening**, what is the **supply-chain** risk of unpinned or unverified third-party dependencies?

options.text: Compromised upstream packages or typo-squatted dependencies can execute malicious code during build or runtime

questions.prompt: Select all essential steps when **rotating a compromised secret**. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Generate and deploy the new secret to runtime secret stores
Verify services work with the new credential
Audit access logs for unauthorized usage during the exposure window

questions.prompt: What is **MTTR** (Mean Time To Recovery) vs **MTTF** (Mean Time To Failure)?

options.text: MTTF is time to deploy CSS
MTTR measures average time to restore service after an outage; MTTF measures average uptime between failures

questions.prompt: What does **distributed tracing** (`trace_id` + `span_id` via W3C `traceparent`) unlock?

options.text: Visualizing the exact call tree and per-hop latency across multiple services for a single request

questions.prompt: Why do SRE teams run **GameDays** or controlled **Chaos Engineering** experiments?

options.text: To delete production data without backups
To verify backups, failovers, alerts, and runbooks actually work under realistic failure before a real outage hits

questions.prompt: What is **blast radius** in operations?

options.text: The maximum scope of users, services, or regions affected if a change or failure goes wrong

questions.prompt: How do **feature flags** improve production reliability?

options.text: They remove the need for tests
They decouple code deployment from feature release, allowing instant kill-switch rollback without redeploying

questions.prompt: Match each resilience pattern to the failure it mitigates.

columns.label: Prevents one slow tenant/endpoint from exhausting shared thread/connection pools
Protects origin capacity from traffic spikes or abusive clients
Prevents sockets from hanging indefinitely on stalled upstreams

questions.prompt: What is the danger of **missing timeouts** on outbound HTTP or DB calls?

options.text: A hung upstream silently ties up goroutines/threads and connection pools until the entire service freezes

questions.prompt: What does `openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates` check?

options.text: The live TLS certificate's `notBefore` and `notAfter` expiration dates

questions.prompt: Why should **backup restores** be tested periodically on an isolated environment?

options.text: An untested backup is an assumption — silent corruption, missing permissions, or wrong encryption keys only show up on restore

questions.prompt: What do **RPO** and **RTO** measure in disaster recovery? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: RPO = max acceptable data loss (time since last backup)
RTO = max acceptable downtime to restore service
RPO = total RAM per cluster node

questions.prompt: In Linux security hardening, what does checking `ss -tulpn` and disabling unused services achieve?

options.text: Reduces exposed network attack surface by closing unnecessary listening ports

questions.prompt: Select all **reliability anti-patterns** to eliminate in production services. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Sharing one database user with superuser rights across all apps
Using structured health checks and graceful shutdown
Swallowing errors silently (`catch (_) {}`) without logging or metrics
Retrying non-idempotent POST payments without an idempotency key

questions.prompt: What is **multi-window, multi-burn-rate SLO alerting**?

options.text: Alerting when the error budget is burning fast enough across short and long windows to threaten the SLO, catching fast outages without paging on tiny blips
Sending alerts only once a year

questions.prompt: What does `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' https://example.com` output?

options.text: Only the HTTP status code and total request duration in seconds — handy for quick CLI latency checks

questions.prompt: Why should **automated patching** of OS/runtime security updates be staged (dev -> staging -> canary -> prod)?

options.text: To delay security fixes for years
To catch breaking ABI/library changes before rolling out across all production nodes at once

questions.prompt: What is **read-only root filesystem** (`--read-only` / `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`) in hardened containers?

options.text: Prevents the app from reading config
Prevents processes from modifying binaries or dropping malware onto the container root filesystem at runtime

questions.prompt: What is **log redaction / PII scrubbing**?

options.text: Stripping or masking tokens, passwords, credit cards, and sensitive user fields before logs leave the service

questions.prompt: How do **synthetic probes / blackbox checks** complement internal application metrics?

options.text: They test end-to-end reachability (DNS, TLS, CDN, proxy, app) from external user locations even if internal metrics stop

questions.prompt: Match each security hardening control to its layer.
Select all useful checks during initial **high-latency incident triage**. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Inspect downstream dependencies (DB query time, cache hit rate, third-party APIs)
Check host/pod saturation (CPU throttling, connection pool exhaustion, GC pauses)
Check if latency jumped after a recent deploy or config/feature-flag change

questions.prompt: What does `govulncheck ./...` or `npm audit --omit=dev` help automate in TechOps?

options.text: Detecting known vulnerabilities in production dependencies early in CI/CD

questions.prompt: Why is **log retention & rotation** (`logrotate` / cloud lifecycle rules) mandatory on production hosts?

options.text: Logs are only stored in RAM
Unbounded logs eventually fill 100% of disk, crashing databases and services

questions.prompt: What is the defining mindset of **Site Reliability Engineering (SRE)**?

options.text: Treating operations as a software engineering problem: automating toil, measuring SLOs, and designing resilient systems
